mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that may lead the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between CPI increases and subsequent negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in Real Final Sales of 1% or more month-over-month signals weakening consumer demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between RSAFS declines and subsequent negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and subsequent negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in Industrial Production (INDPRO) signals supply-side constraints that may lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO declines and subsequent negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is above 3% year-over-year, the real interest rate is negative, signaling an inflationary environment that leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between negative real rates and subsequent negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and falling housing starts (HOUST) signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of rising unemployment and falling housing starts on subsequent negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 300,000 in a month, it signals strong labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between strong PAYEMS growth and subsequent positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, when the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increases by more than 0.5% in a quarter, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and subsequent negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
